segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And for this reason, the Samaritans accept only the Torah.
And it is said
that this same Ezra
wrote the Torah in the Aramaic script, that is, Syriac.
And this is the Peshitta version that is in the hands of the Syrians.
And in the sixth year of Hezekiah, Sennacherib began to reign over the Assyrians, who went up against Jerusalem;
and by the prayer of Hezekiah he was defeated;
and fifteen years were added to the life of Hezekiah.
For the angel of the Lord killed one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of Sennacherib.
And he also heard that Tirhakah {OCR?}, king of the Cushites, had set out to fight against him;
and immediately he departed to Nineveh,
and there his sons killed him.
And Hezekiah made a pool of water,
and made a conduit for the city of Jerusalem,
and brought water in through pipes.
And when he showed the envoys of the king of Babylon all that was in his house,
the Lord was angry,
and it was said to him:
"All that they have seen in your house, and your sons, shall be eunuchs, that is, eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon."
And Hezekiah said:
"Good is the word of the Lord;
if only there may be peace in my days."
And in his days,
Tobit the righteous, from the captivity of Israel, while living in Nineveh,
received good tidings from the angel Raphael;
and the blindness of his eyes was healed by the gall of the fish that was given by the angel.
And at this time Syracuse,
and Catania,
and Leontinoi,
and Megara, and Martonia,
and Taormina (?), and Chersonesus (?) were built in Sicily.
And Sennacherib built Tarsus of Cilicia.
After Hezekiah, Manasseh his son reigned fifty-five years.
And in his thirteenth year, he killed Isaiah the prophet, sawing him in two with a saw.
And on this account, God rejected him,
and delivered him into the hands of the Assyrians.
And when they took him into captivity and bound him with harsh irons,
they placed him in a bronze statue of a beast in Nineveh.
And when the distress grew severe upon him,
he turned to the God of his fathers,
and offered true repentance,
and prayed that famous prayer.
And God answered him,
and he was delivered and returned to Jerusalem.
And that four-faced image {OCR?} [Footnote: 24 Mar Dionysius, the chronicler: the names of these cities were written in Greek here.]
